card: Bitcoin Core gains descriptor policy inspection and multisig safety verification via AnalyzeDescriptor, exposed through a verbose option on getdescriptorinfo and a new analyzedescriptor wallet RPC. Currently, participants joining a multisig wallet cannot verify with Core whether a coordinator-provided descriptor enforces the agreed k-of-n policy without trapdoors such as repeated cosigner keys or active key-path spending. The analysis warns about structural issues without rejecting descriptors, while the wallet RPC correlates keys against the wallet and confirms address derivation even when locked. This PR depends on PR 35918 and advances the multisig setup workflow tracked in issue 35645.
changed_since_previous: Added dedicated release notes in doc/release-notes-36885.md detailing the new analyzedescriptor RPC and getdescriptorinfo verbose argument.
evidence: PR description: 'Before importing a multisig descriptor received from a coordinator, each participant needs to check that it is the setup they agreed on: a k-of-n where any k cosigners can spend and nothing else can, that their own key is in it, and that they all derived the same first address. Today nothing in Core reports what a descriptor commits to, so tools had to parse the descriptor string by hand, as the multisig wizard in #36325 (now closed) did.'

Commit bcb40c7444: 'Two cosigner slots are the same holder if they share a root key, derive the same key at the first address, or one is the other's unhardened child xpub... Core accepts such descriptors, and fewer signers than the threshold can spend from them.'
problem: When participating in a collaborative multisig wallet setup, participants must ensure that a descriptor provided by an external coordinator adheres strictly to the agreed k-of-n spending policy, contains their key, and generates matching addresses. Bitcoin Core had no mechanism to inspect descriptor spending policies or verify multisig safety invariants, forcing external tools and setup wizards to parse descriptor strings manually and risking acceptance of configurations where duplicate keys or unconstrained key paths reduce effective security thresholds.

risk.why: A bug in multisig safety analysis or wallet key matching could misinform users or automated tools about whether a descriptor is safe to import or can be signed by the loaded wallet.

scope_notes: The PR incorporates the first three commits from PR #35918 and inspection commits adapted from w0xlt's descriptor inspection branch. A large portion of the lines added consists of tests and fuzzing fixtures across descriptor, RPC, and wallet test files.
summary: Adds descriptor inspection, policy parsing, and multisig verification to Bitcoin Core. The core analysis parses key expressions and policies to verify whether a descriptor conforms to a recognized k-of-n multisig setup without unintended spending paths or repeated cosigners. These capabilities are exposed via a new verbose parameter on getdescriptorinfo and a new analyzedescriptor wallet RPC that additionally identifies owned keys, signing capability, and first receive address.
